Description: A short descriptive name for this analytical procedure, with version number. Should include instrument/mass-analyzer configuration, technique, and target mineral or isotopic system.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'LA-ICP-MS U-Pb Zircon Geochronology v1' | 'LA-SF-ICP-MS U-Th-Pb Monazite Geochronology v1'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Top-level analytical technique identifier, including the ICP-MS mass-analyzer configuration used for in situ U-(Th-)Pb dating.
Example/Allowed Content: LA-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | LA-Q-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | LA-SF-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | LA-MC-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Person(s) or laboratory responsible for developing and registering this procedure. ORCID recommended for individuals.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'M. Horstwood (ORCID: 0000-0002-9720-716X), NERC Isotope Geosciences Laboratory'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Name(s) of the analyst(s) who performed the analysis session. ORCID recommended for persistent identification.
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Name of the laboratory or institution hosting the instrument. Standard cross-TAPP identity field, distinct from the paper-sourced 'Laboratory name' field above.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NERC Isotope Geosciences Laboratory, British Geological Survey'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs). Merged 2026-07-27: also covers Table 3's 'Laboratory name' item (paper example: 'Dept of Earth Science, University of Everywhere').

Description: Persistent identifier for the laboratory, e.g., ROR ID.
Example/Allowed Content: ROR ID or equivalent URI (https://ror.org/)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: First date this procedure configuration was used in production.
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Date on which the analytical session began. For sessions spanning multiple days, use the date of the first session.
Example/Allowed Content: YYYY-MM-DD
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Date on which the analytical session ended. May equal Analysis Start Date for single-day sessions.
Example/Allowed Content: YYYY-MM-DD
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: DOI or unique persistent identifier for the registered procedure used in this analysis. Mandatory when submitting analytical data, to encourage formal procedure registration. Enter 'pending' if applied for but not yet minted.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., http://doi.org/10.60520/IEDA/114187 | pending
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Grants and other funding sources that supported instrument purchase, major upgrades, and procedure development. Include grant numbers and funding agencies.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NERC IP-1332-0512' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Grants and other funding sources that supported the specific sample analyses reported here. Distinct from procedure development funding, which may have been awarded years earlier.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NSF EAR-1524297' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: DOI or URL for peer-reviewed publications or technical reports describing, validating, or benchmarking this procedure.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., doi:10.1111/j.1751-908X.2016.00379.x (Horstwood et al. 2016, community reporting standard)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Other analytical techniques applied to the same sample(s) whose results are intended to be interpreted together with, or used to independently validate, this dataset. Enter 'None' if no coupling is intended.
Example/Allowed Content: CA-ID-TIMS | SIMS | EPMA | CL/BSE Imaging | Other: specify | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Describes (1) the functional relationship between this dataset and the coupled technique, and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique was performed first and why. Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not 'None'.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'A subset of dated grains were subsequently analysed by CA-ID-TIMS to independently validate the LA-ICP-MS age population; CA-ID-TIMS performed after LA-ICP-MS screening identified target grains'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Registered procedure DOI for the coupled technique named above.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., pending | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: DOI or persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication reporting both datasets together.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'same submission' | pending | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Pre-ablation characterisation imaging (typically cathodoluminescence [CL] or backscattered electron [BSE]) used to reveal internal zoning, inherited cores, and metamict domains for selecting valid spot locations, including the imaging instrument and settings used.
Example/Allowed Content: CL, FEI Quanta600, 10 nA, 17 mm working distance

Description: General description of the U-(Th-)Pb-bearing mineral(s) this procedure is designed to analyse. Used for discoverability and procedure matching.
Example/Allowed Content: Zircon | Monazite | Titanite | Apatite | Rutile | Xenotime | Baddeleyite | Perovskite | Allanite | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 2 field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs). Merged 2026-07-27: also covers Table 3's 'Sample type/mineral' item (paper example: 'Detrital zircons').

Description: Standard cross-TAPP description of how samples were prepared for analysis (mounting, polishing, coating, etc.).
Example/Allowed Content: Conventional mineral separation, 1 inch resin mount, 1 µm polish to finish
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 2 field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs). Merged 2026-07-27: replaces Table 3's separate 'Sample preparation' item; example below is Table 3's own value.

Description: Name or identifier of the sample analysed, as used in the laboratory. Should match the identifier used in associated publications or data tables.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NWA 7533 zrn-14' | 'Jack Hills detrital zircon JH-22'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 2 universal field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Globally unique, persistent identifier for the analysed sample. IGSN is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., IGSN: IEDA-100001 (https://www.igsn.org/)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 2 universal field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Metadata Item: Make, Model and Type (Laser Ablation System)
Description: Manufacturer, model, and type of the laser ablation system. Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016) uses the generic header 'Make, Model and type' for both the laser and the ICP-MS instrument; the instrument context has been added in parentheses here so the two fields remain distinguishable outside the original two-column table layout.
Example/Allowed Content: ESI/New Wave Research, UP193FX
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016); disambiguated from the identically-labelled ICP-MS instrument field

Description: Type, design origin, and internal volume of the ablation cell. Cell volume is a primary determinant of aerosol washout time and therefore the achievable time resolution of the data.
Example/Allowed Content: In-house built low volume cell, volume ca. 4 cm³

Description: Manufacturer, model, and mass-analyzer type of the ICP-MS instrument (quadrupole, single-collector sector-field, or multi-collector).
Example/Allowed Content: Nu Instruments, Nu Plasma HR, MC-ICP-MS
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016); disambiguated from the identically-labelled laser ablation system field

Description: Configuration by which the ablated aerosol is delivered to the plasma, including any co-aspirated tracer or spike solution (e.g., a Tl solution used for instrumental mass bias correction, or a ²³⁵U spike used for isotope dilution).
Example/Allowed Content: Ablation aerosol combined with co-aspiration of desolvated Tl-235U tracer

Description: Detector configuration installed in the mass spectrometer used to measure the U-(Th-)Pb isotope beams.
Example/Allowed Content: mixed Faraday-multiple ion counting array

Description: Instrument control and data acquisition software used to collect raw signal data, including version number.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Nu Instruments Nu Plasma TRA 2.x' | 'Thermo Qtegra 2.10' | 'Agilent MassHunter 4.6'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 3 software field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs); Table 3 does not request acquisition software as a distinct item

Description: Software used for signal processing, background subtraction, downhole fractionation correction, and age calculation, including version number.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Iolite 4.7 (Paton et al. 2010)' | 'VizualAge_UcomPbine (Chew et al. 2014)' | 'In-house spreadsheet'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 3 software field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs); see also the paper-sourced 'Data Processing Package Used/Correction for LIEF' field in Group 5

Description: Procedure-level declaration of the analytical mode(s) this procedure covers. This TAPP is scoped to static spot ablation only, consistent with Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016), where the 'Sampling mode/pattern' example is 'Static spot ablation' and depth-profiling/single-pulse ablation is discussed only as a supplementary variant (see 'Other Information'). No mode-flag columns are used in this TAPP because only one mode is in scope.
Example/Allowed Content: Spot Analysis
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 3 (mandatory first field of Group 4 in every TAPP). Merged 2026-07-27: also covers Table 3's 'Sampling mode/pattern' item (paper example: 'Static spot ablation').

Description: Wavelength of the laser used for ablation, in nanometres.
Example/Allowed Content: 193 nm

Description: Duration of each individual laser pulse. A fixed hardware property of the laser system that determines the thermal vs. non-thermal ablation regime.
Example/Allowed Content: 4 ns

Description: Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface, the primary control on ablation rate and crater morphology.
Example/Allowed Content: 2.5 J cm⁻²

Description: Laser pulse repetition rate.
Example/Allowed Content: 5 Hz

Description: Total on-sample ablation time per spot, as set in the acquisition method.

Depth of the ablation pit produced under the registered laser conditions, the method used to measure it, and the resulting per-pulse ablation rate. Characterises the achievable depth/time resolution of the procedure.
Example/Allowed Content: 16 µm pit depth, measured using an optical microscope, SEM and interferometry, equivalent to 0.08 µm/pulse

Description: Diameter of the laser spot as set in the acquisition method (nominal) and as independently measured on the sample or a test material (actual).
Example/Allowed Content: 25 µm/32 µm

Description: Identity and plumbing configuration of the gas used to transport the ablated aerosol from the cell to the torch.
Example/Allowed Content: 100% He in the cell, Ar make-up gas combined using a Y-piece 50% along the sample transport line to the torch.

Description: Flow rate of the carrier gas through the ablation cell.
Example/Allowed Content: 0.8 L min⁻¹

Description: ICP radiofrequency forward power.
Source and estimated flow rate of any make-up gas added downstream of the ablation cell, including any desolvating nebuliser used for tracer co-aspiration.
Example/Allowed Content: Sourced from Nu Instruments DSN-100 desolvating nebuliser. Neb pressure 24 psi (estimated at 0.7 L min⁻¹) Ar.

Description: Mass-to-charge positions (isotope masses) this procedure is designed to measure. Defines the scope of the procedure; the analyst may record the specific subset actually measured in a given session.

Metadata Item: Integration Time per Peak/Dwell Times; Quadrupole Settling Time Between Mass Jumps
Description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope, and the settling time allowed between mass jumps, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016).
Example/Allowed Content: 200 ms for each isotope

Metadata Item: Total Integration Time per Output Data Point (s)
Description: Total duty-cycle time for one complete mass-scan sweep (sum of all per-isotope dwell times and settling times), which sets the time resolution of the down-hole signal.
Example/Allowed Content: ~1.2 s (N.B. this should represent the time resolution of the data)

Description: Instrument sensitivity expressed as useful yield — the percentage of sampled atoms of a given element that are ultimately detected as ions — for the analytical session, following the method cited.
Example/Allowed Content: 0.4% U ((#ions detected/#atoms sampled)*100; Schaltegger et al. 2015)

Description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in dead-time correction of high count rates.
Example/Allowed Content: 6, 9 and 7 ns IC0, IC1 and IC2 resp.

Description: Supplementary methodological context not captured by the structured fields above, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016) — in the source paper's own example, notes on ablation-cell and sample-line configuration for depth-profiling/single-pulse ablation studies, a variant not otherwise in scope for this single-mode (Spot Analysis) TAPP.
Example/Allowed Content: Depth profiling and single-pulse ablation studies used a low-volume ablation cell, sample line of 3 m from ablation cell to torch and a 20 s wait time between ablations. Cell washout time was ca. 0.8 s to 1% of peak signal.

Description: Duration of the background (gas blank) measurement and how it is applied to correct the ablation signal.
Example/Allowed Content: 30 s on-peak zero subtracted

Metadata Item: Data Processing Package Used/Correction for LIEF
Description: Software used for data reduction and the method (if any) used to correct for laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF), as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016). Bundles software identity together with the LIEF correction assumption/method in a single field, per the paper's own field structure.
Example/Allowed Content: Nu Instruments Nu Plasma TRA software and in-house spreadsheet for data normalisation, uncertainty propagation and age calculation. LIEF correction assumes reference material and samples behave identically.

Description: Method used to correct measured isotope ratios for instrumental mass bias (mass discrimination).
Example/Allowed Content: Tl-U tracer solution used for initial mass bias correction with 207Pb/206Pb and 206Pb/238U additionally normalised to reference material

Description: Whether a common-Pb correction was applied, and if so, the model composition (e.g., Stacey and Kramers 1975) and its uncertainty used in the correction.
Example/Allowed Content: No common-Pb correction applied to the data.

Description: Uncertainty level at which ages/ratios are quoted (e.g., 1σ, 2σ) and the method used to propagate component uncertainties (e.g., quadratic addition) into the final reported value.
Example/Allowed Content: Ages are quoted at 2s absolute, propagation is by quadratic addition. Reproducibility and age uncertainty of reference material and common-Pb composition uncertainty are propagated where appropriate.

Description: Names the primary calibration reference material and the secondary/validation reference material(s) used in the session.
Example/Allowed Content: 91500 used as primary reference material, Plesovice and GJ1 used as secondaries/validation

Description: Accepted isotopic values and source citation for each reference material named in Calibration Strategy.
Example/Allowed Content: 91500 (Wiedenbeck et al. 1995); Plesovice (Slama et al. 2008); GJ1 206Pb/238U 0.097877 ± 0.07%, 207Pb/206Pb 0.060171 ± 0.08% (in-house CA-TIMS, this study)

Description: Session validation results: the weighted-average age, uncertainty, MSWD, and n obtained for each secondary/validation reference material analysed as an unknown, plus the systematic uncertainty value applied in propagation.
Example/Allowed Content: Plesovice – Wtd ave 206Pb/238U age = 338 ± 3 (2s, MSWD = 0.9, n = 8); GJ-1 – Wtd ave 206Pb/238U age = 602 ± 5 (2s, MSWD = 1.1, n = 7); Systematic uncertainty for propagation is 2% (2s).

Description: Session detection limit for U, Th, and/or Pb, demonstrating the reliability of reported concentrations near the detection limit. Not requested by Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016), which focuses on age uncertainty rather than elemental detection limits.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '0.05 ppm U (3σ background)' | 'Range: 0.02–0.4 ppm across U, Th, Pb'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 6 QC term (gap vs. Table 3)

Description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the session detection limit reported above.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '3σ of background ion counts per Longerich et al. (1996)'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 6 QC term (gap vs. Table 3)
